requirement: For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.
rationale:
I found no gap against the text of `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`.

**Obligations and code**
- **Delivery through the `SessionStart` hook.** The hook is registered in `Cargo.toml` metadata (`package.metadata.symposium.hooks`, event `SessionStart`, args `hook session-start`). `src/main.rs#fn[main]` routes that command to `hook::session_start`. The registration carries an {impl} of `symposium_setup_hook`, and this requirement cites that hook rather than redefining it.
- **Applicability.** `src/hook.rs#fn[session_start]` is the {impl} root. It calls `session_start_response`, which returns `{"SessionStart": {}}`, meaning no context, when `setup::find_project_root` finds no project. It does the same when `setup::project_depends_on_habeas` is false.
  - I did not read `setup::project_depends_on_habeas`, but tests cover its `[dependencies]`-only case.
  - Agent context is therefore added only inside a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under dev-dependencies.
- **Nonblocking context.** The response is `{"SessionStart": {"additionalContext": ...}}` with no blocking or decision field.
- **Exactly one sentence pointing to the skill.** The context starts from the constant `SKILL_SENTENCE`: "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." That sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill before starting work.
  - The setup advisory, appended only when `setup::is_configured` is false, never mentions the skill. The skill sentence is therefore the only one that points to it.

**Tests**
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_points_to_the_habeas_skill_once_setup_is_complete]` runs `habeas setup`, then checks that the whole response, from the project root and from a nested directory, equals the skill sentence alone. This covers the `configured` example.
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_puts_the_skill_sentence_before_the_setup_advisory]` covers an incomplete project. It asserts a single `additionalContext`, the skill sentence first, then the advisory, and exactly one "`habeas` skill" mention.
- `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py#def[main]` exercises the real Symposium delivery path for both the incomplete and the configured states.
- Tests that carry no {test} reference to this subject also cover its boundaries. These are `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_gives_no_context_outside_habeas_projects]` (no project, and `habeas` only under `[dependencies]`) and `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_advises_only_when_setup_is_incomplete]`. Those obligations are specified by `.not_applicable` and `.setup_state`, whose {impl} sits on the same `session_start` node.

**Unspecified behavior**
The advisory text and the `SessionStart` JSON wrapper fall within what the requirements describe.

text: :::{req} symposium_skill_hook

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.
:::{req} setup

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
:::{req} symposium_setup_hook

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive a Symposium `SessionStart` hook. The hook MUST check whether the configuration and files required by `requirements.cli.setup` are present and compatible. If not, it MUST provide nonblocking agent context saying that Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. If setup is complete or no applicable project is found, it MUST provide no setup advisory. The hook MUST NOT modify project files or run setup itself.
:::{req} overview_skill

Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
:::{example} symposium_skill_hook.configured

In a project where `habeas setup` has completed, the whole session-start agent context is one sentence such as "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`
:::{example} symposium_skill_hook.configured

In a project where `habeas setup` has completed, the whole session-start agent context is one sentence such as "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`
:::{example} symposium_skill_hook.incomplete_setup

In a project that lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]` but has no `habeas.css` in its book source directory, the agent context starts with the skill sentence, followed by the advisory saying Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.setup_state`
:::{req} symposium_skill_hook.not_applicable
When a session starts outside every Cargo and mdBook project, or within one whose manifest does not list `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, the hook MUST provide no agent context.
:::{example} symposium_skill_hook.runtime_dependency_only

A Cargo and mdBook project that lists `habeas` only under `[dependencies]` gets no session-start agent context, neither the skill sentence nor a setup advisory. {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook.not_applicable`
:::{req} symposium_skill_hook.setup_state

When the setup advisory of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook` also applies, the hook MUST provide the sentence of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` and the advisory together in one agent context, with the sentence first.
